definition: A foundational SQL clause specifying which columns or expressions should be returned by a query.
The SQL clause declaring the source table, view, or subquery containing the requested data.
A filtering clause that restricts rows before any grouping or aggregation takes place.

A filter clause operating strictly on aggregated summary rows after GROUP BY execution.
A clause ordering result rows in ascending or descending order based on specified expressions.
A clause restricting the maximum number of rows returned in the final result set.
A clause that skips a designated number of rows before beginning to return records.
A keyword eliminating duplicate rows from the query output, returning only unique value combinations.
A relational join returning only rows with matching join keys across both participating tables.
example: orders INNER JOIN users ON orders.user_id = users.id;

definition: A join returning all rows from the left table and matched rows from the right table.
example: customers LEFT JOIN orders ON customers.id = orders.customer_id;

definition: A join returning all rows from the right table and matching records from the left table.
example: sales RIGHT JOIN products ON sales.sku = products.sku;

definition: A join returning all rows whenever a match exists in either the left or right table.
example: FULL OUTER JOIN suppliers ON products.supplier_id = suppliers.id;

definition: A Cartesian product join pairing every row of the first table with all rows of the second table.
example: SELECT * FROM colors CROSS JOIN sizes;

definition: A regular join where a table is joined against itself using distinct table aliases.
example: employees e JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.id;

definition: A set operator combining rows from two queries and automatically removing duplicate records.
example: SELECT city FROM clients UNION SELECT city FROM leads;

definition: A set operator combining rows from two queries while retaining all duplicate rows for maximum speed.
example: SELECT id FROM jan_orders UNION ALL SELECT id FROM feb_orders;

definition: A set operator returning only distinct rows appearing simultaneously in both query outputs.
example: SELECT user_id FROM q1_buyers INTERSECT SELECT user_id FROM q2_buyers;

definition: A set operator returning distinct rows from the first query that do not exist in the second query.
example: SELECT id FROM signups EXCEPT SELECT id FROM churns;

definition: A temporary named result set defined within a WITH statement to simplify complex multi-step queries.
example: WITH monthly AS (SELECT ...) SELECT * FROM monthly;

definition: A nested query embedded inside an outer SELECT, FROM, or WHERE clause to produce intermediate results.
A subquery referencing columns in the outer query, evaluating once per outer table candidate row.

definition: A boolean operator testing whether a subquery returns at least one row, stopping on first match.

definition: Database systems designed to process large volumes of fast, simple transactional queries like payments and order lookups.
example: Bank account ledger databases processing atomic writes;

definition: Database systems optimized for complex multi-table aggregations, analytical queries, and business intelligence reporting across historical data.
example: Aggregating 500 million transaction rows across dimensions;

definition: A data modeling technique managing how historical changes to dimension entity attributes are tracked over time.
example: SCD Type 1 (overwrite) vs SCD Type 2 (historical rows with validity dates);

definition: An SCD approach overwriting old attribute values with new data, maintaining no historical record of previous states.
example: Updating a customer's current phone number;

definition: An SCD approach inserting a new record with effective start/end dates and flags whenever attribute modifications occur.
example: Tracking historical customer city changes for regional sales attribution;

definition: A synthetic artificial primary key (e.g. integer or UUID) assigned to dimension tables independent of business keys.
A business identifier assigned to an entity in operational source systems (e.g. employee number or PAN).
example: Using natural PAN numbers or GSTIN codes;

definition: A focused subset of an enterprise data warehouse designed to serve the analytical needs of a specific business department.
example: Marketing data mart containing campaign and attribution tables;

definition: The lifecycle tracking map showing the complete historical path, origins, and transformations data undergoes across pipelines.
example: Visualizing source CRM tables feeding final finance dashboards;

definition: An organized inventory of enterprise data assets providing metadata, data definitions, owners, and search capabilities.
example: Alation, Collibra, or Amundsen metadata portals;

definition: Structured data providing descriptive, administrative, or structural information regarding underlying enterprise data assets.
example: Schema definitions, column descriptions, and update timestamps;

definition: The formal framework of policies, processes, and security controls ensuring data accuracy, privacy, and compliance.
example: Enforcing role-based access control and DPDP compliance;

definition: An open-source, columnar storage file format providing efficient data compression and fast columnar encoding schemes.
A simple plain-text delimited format where values are separated by commas, widely used for data exchange.
example: Exporting spreadsheet rows to plain .csv files;

definition: A lightweight semi-structured data interchange format storing data as key-value pairs and nested array objects.
example: Parsing nested API payload response documents;

definition: An open-source orchestration workflow platform used to author, schedule, and programmatically monitor complex data pipelines.
example: DAGs defining dependencies between pipeline task operators;

definition: A mathematical graph of data pipeline tasks connected by directional execution dependencies with no circular loops.
example: Airflow pipeline orchestrating extract -> transform -> validate;

definition: A design pattern identifying and capturing individual database row modifications (inserts, updates, deletes) in real time.
example: Debezium streaming Postgres WAL logs into Kafka;

definition: A distributed event streaming platform handling real-time high-throughput messaging between distributed source and target applications.
example: Streaming real-time order events into analytics engines;

definition: The continuous real-time computation and aggregation of data records immediately as individual events occur.
example: Flink or Spark Streaming calculating real-time fraud alerts;

definition: The scheduled execution of data transformation jobs across accumulated blocks of data at periodic calendar intervals.
example: Nightly batch jobs processing daily sales summaries;

definition: A pipeline property guaranteeing that executing an operation multiple times produces the exact same state as running it once.
example: INSERT OVERWRITE partitions preventing duplicate rows upon rerun;

definition: Dividing large database tables into smaller physical chunks based on key columns (e.g. date) to accelerate query performance.
A horizontal scaling architecture distributing database rows across multiple independent physical server nodes.
example: Sharding customer data across geographical database clusters;

definition: An automated software process extracting data from source systems, transforming data structures, and loading into destinations.
example: Automating raw clickstream ingestion into reporting marts;

definition: Automated validation checks verifying data freshness, schema adherence, null constraints, and unique integrity before consumption.
example: Running dbt test for not_null and unique keys;

definition: The monitoring capability to understand data health across freshness, volume, distribution, schema drift, and lineage anomalies.
example: Monte Carlo monitoring unexpected table drop alerts;

definition: An operational incident occurring when a data pipeline fails to deliver validated data within agreed business deadline windows.
example: Reporting table failing to refresh prior to 8 AM executive review;

definition: The process of re-running data pipelines across historical date ranges to apply updated transformation logic or new fields.
example: Backfilling 12 months of newly engineered churn indicators;

definition: A cloud data warehouse capability creating instant logical clones of databases or tables without duplicating underlying physical storage files.
example: Snowflake zero-copy cloning for staging testing environments;

definition: A software approach allowing applications to query multiple disparate data sources as a single unified logical data view without moving data.
example: Querying data lakes and relational DBs seamlessly;

definition: A technical professional bridging data analysts and data engineers, writing production-grade dbt transformations and data models.
example: Transforming raw source tables into clean reporting marts;
